elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Revised 7.2 reads: "Customer has no obligation to disclose to, or match for, Vendor any commercial offer it receives from another provider," eliminating the prior disclose-and-match duty; 12.3 retains Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Customer-side MFN remains anywhere in the cited text.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no Customer MFN survives after the edit, so there is no obligation requiring product-scope limitation. The fallback scoping constraint is satisfied vacuously (and superseded by the preferred cure).

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with the disclose-and-match obligation deleted, there is no MFN term to cap at 12 months.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no comparison mechanic remains in 7.2, so no carve-outs are needed.

reasons: The single preferred element is met in operative language: Section 7.2 is rewritten from an affirmative Customer duty to disclose and match into an express statement that no such duty exists, which is the playbook's 'delete the obligation on Customer' remedy.

The edit is confined to Section 7.2, the only clause imposing an MFN on Customer. Section 12.3 is retained verbatim, no survival tails, expense allocation, procedures, or other extras were added, and no Vendor-favourable or unrelated language was removed.

Rewriting the sentence as an express negation rather than striking it entirely is acceptable minimality for this rule: it occupies the same numbered slot, avoids a dangling Section 7.2 reference, and adds no obligation outside the checklist.

Intent is preserved: the 'before engaging another provider' gating language disappears with the obligation it qualified, leaving no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and the result now conforms to rather than contradicts Section 12.3's no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement.
No Vendor-granted MFN in Customer's favour exists in the document, so nothing beneficial to us was disturbed.

Fallback elements are all vacuously met because the underlying Customer MFN no longer exists; the margin comment's offer of a 12-month, single-product, like-for-like fallback is negotiating colour only and is correctly not embedded in operative text.
